stock.reason: The stock build last published for 2026-10-06, not today. A pick belongs to the session it was made in, so it is not repeated here.
stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.

stories.title: OpenAI agents tried to hack Wikipedia tools and flooded it with traffic
stories.excerpt: The reports of OpenAI agents harming third-party sites keep coming.
stories.lead:
The publisher of Wikipedia said Monday that OpenAI agents attempted to hack a note-taking tool it hosts, made unauthorized edits, and sent millions of resource-intensive requests to its infrastructure, in the latest instance of OpenAI systems taking harmful and potentially dangerous actions.

The objective of some of the OpenAI agents’ actions, the Wikimedia Foundation said, was to use Wikipedia as a proxy for fetching data from third-party sites. In one case, the agents posted “malicious edits” that were intended to repurpose a citation tool as a proxy. In another, the agents made unsuccessful attempts to compromise the Wikipedia Etherpad note-taking tool so it would serve the same purpose.

stories.title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry
stories.excerpt: The prize was given to the French and Japanese scientists for solving the mystery of life's asymmetry.
stories.lead:
The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for providing a solution to the chemical mystery of life's asymmetry.

The Nobel Committee explained: "Molecules used by all life, such as the amino acids that are building of proteins, are what is known as chiral.

"This means that they have two versions that are mirror images of one another."

stories.title: India's first bank rate hike since 2023 signals growing inflation concerns
stories.excerpt: The hike reflects a global shift towards tighter monetary policy as central banks battle inflation fuelled by Middle East conflict.
stories.lead:
In his post-policy address, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said the decision reflected challenging geopolitical developments, even as the Indian economy remained strong.

He said cuts were "off the table for now", with the central bank likely to either raise rates further or keep them unchanged to contain inflation.

The RBI projects Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation at 5.2% for 2026-27 - higher than the 5% estimated earlier - to account for price pressure due to weather disruptions, weak monsoon and high volatility in international oil prices.

stories.excerpt: Midterm candidates are talking up Medicare for All, and in a poll 2 out of 3 Americans said they support it. The phrase speaks to a desire for radical change, though many don't really know what it is.
stories.lead:
Christina Starks-Clay doesn't know how "Medicare for All" would work exactly, but she's willing to bet it'd be better than what she has now.

While standing in line for a Sept. 11 town hall for U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Lansing, she whipped out her phone and pulled up a screenshot.

It was of the $1,000 cashier's check she'd picked up at the bank that day to pay down a chunk of her son's dental bills.

stories.lead:
Royal Mail plans to cut up to 2,500 jobs by the end of next year, as it struggles with a slump in letters being sent and seeks to compete in the cutthroat parcel delivery market.

To simplify its processes and save money, Royal has carried out a review of its head office and support functions, and will reduce them by “up to 2,500” – less than 2% of its workforce of more than 131,000 people, it said.

The company, owned since April 2025 by the Czech billionaire Daniel Křetínský, hopes to achieve the reductions through “natural attrition” (people leaving anyway) and voluntary redundancies, without the need for compulsory redundancies.

stories.title: Carpetbagger allegation, misplaced valor make Nevada's safe red House seat competitive
stories.excerpt: Northern Nevada has a reliably red congressional seat, represented by a Republican since it was drawn in the early 1980s. A complicated candidate and a potential blue wave this year could change that.
stories.lead:
RENO, Nev. — The race for Nevada's 2nd Congressional District shouldn't be competitive, just based on history and math. But the Republican Party's nominee, David Flippo, is facing an unusually tough race despite having President Trump's endorsement, bogged down by allegations that he exaggerated his military service and lacks real ties to the district.

"This seat is some kind of competitive like it has never been in the history since it was created," said Mark Amodei, the retiring Republican congressman who has represented the northern Nevada district for the past 15 years. "And you know what I attribute that to? I attribute it to the candidate and the way he's run his campaign."
